messages:
Maya Patel: quick idea — propose a per-pool "hedging window" that widens when eviction rate spikes. soft-drain denies new requests but lets streaming tokens finish and hands off session tokens to fallback pool.
Liam Chen: sounds similar to fast-fail then requeue? how do we avoid a thundering requeue when the backup pool is also preemptible?
Maya Patel: two parts: 1) graded hedging window: pools have a score based on current evict-rate, recent failover, and capacity headroom; higher score => shorter window. 2) token handoff: stream sender attaches a short-lived resume token that the fallback node can use to continue the KV-cache without full warmup.
Sophia Ortiz: measurement question — what's the expected extra cost of holding streams open vs immediate requeueing? we need a cost model to decide thresholds.
Kai Nguyen: implementation sketch:
```
onPreemptNotice(pool):
  score = computePoolScore(pool)
  window = clamp(base_window * (1/score), min, max)
  setPoolSoftDrain(pool, window)
  emit resume_token for open streams
```
Devops Bot: cloud provider termination notices vary 30-120s; use provider signal + node agent heartbeat to start hedging earlier when signal seen.
Liam Chen: if resume_token replay needs warm KV, how do we avoid cold-start amplification on the fallback?
Maya Patel: resume_token contains minimal state: prefix id, last_kv_seq. fallback will request KV snapshot for small prefix and fast-forward. We keep prefix cache TTL short for idle prefixes to control memory.
Sophia Ortiz: add: metric flavors — requeue_rate, resume_success, tail_p90_latency, cost_delta. run A/B with canary pools before global flip.
Kai Nguyen: also recommend capped concurrent resumes per fallback node + exponential backoff to avoid overloading.
Oncall Bot: note: rolling alert rule 4/5 triggered for preemptible pool us-west-2a last night — spike correlates with batch job churn.
Maya Patel: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with the score formula, token format, and proposed metrics. want reviewers: @Liam, @Sophia, @Kai. planning doc due EOD Thurs.
Liam Chen: ack, I'll add simulation harness to the repo and run worst-case spike tests.
Sophia Ortiz: happy to own the cost/metric dashboards.
Kai Nguyen: will prototype token handshake and a small handler for fallback fast-path.
Maya Patel: thanks — keeping this lightweight so ops can roll it to dedicated/dynamic pools fast. :rocket:
